en.question: In an orchestrator-worker design, why is explicit context passing to each worker preferred over letting workers share the orchestrator's full conversation?

options.text: A narrow per-worker context keeps windows small and workers independently testable.
Workers are prohibited from reading conversation history for security reasons.
options.note: It is a context-hygiene design choice, not an access restriction.

options.text: The Messages API does not permit message history to be shared across calls.
options.note: You may send any history you like; nothing forbids it.

options.text: Sharing one context would force the workers to execute strictly sequentially.
options.note: Execution concurrency is independent of what context you pass.

en.explanation: Context isolation is the structural benefit of the pattern. A purpose-built context per worker holds token cost down, removes irrelevant material that degrades focus, and makes each worker a unit you can evaluate alone.
